sources.justification: The US Geological Survey is the authoritative publisher of earthquake magnitude, PAGER impact, and volcanic hazard data.
sources.label: USGS

sources.justification: The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration is the authoritative publisher of climate, atmospheric CO2, and space-weather measurements.
sources.label: NOAA

sources.justification: NASA is the authoritative publisher of near-Earth object survey and planetary defense figures.
sources.label: NASA

sources.justification: NASA's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies is the canonical source for impact-probability figures; a finer label than nasa.gov, which it also matches as a subdomain.
sources.label: NASA CNEOS

sources.justification: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory publishes the orbital determination data behind CNEOS; a finer label than nasa.gov.
sources.label: NASA JPL

sources.justification: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change is the UN body whose assessment reports are the reference for attributed warming figures.
sources.label: IPCC

sources.justification: The Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services is the IPCC's counterpart for biodiversity assessment.
sources.label: IPBES

sources.justification: The World Health Organization is the UN specialized agency for outbreak case counts and public-health emergency declarations.
sources.label: WHO

sources.justification: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention publishes authoritative epidemiological surveillance data.
sources.label: CDC

sources.justification: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control is the EU counterpart to the CDC; a finer label than europa.eu, which it also matches as a subdomain.
sources.label: ECDC

sources.justification: The International Atomic Energy Agency is the UN body for nuclear safety and safeguards reporting.
sources.label: IAEA

sources.justification: The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute is an independent institute established by the Swedish Parliament and the canonical public reference for global nuclear-arsenal and military-expenditure figures. IAEA, the only other nuclear entry, does not publish arsenal counts.
sources.label: SIPRI

sources.justification: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization is the authoritative source for food security and agricultural production figures.
sources.label: FAO

sources.justification: The UN World Food Programme publishes operational hunger and food-crisis figures.
sources.label: UN World Food Programme

sources.justification: The UN Environment Programme is the UN authority on environmental and resource assessment.
sources.label: UN Environment Programme

sources.justification: The International Energy Agency is the intergovernmental authority on energy supply and demand statistics.
sources.label: IEA

sources.justification: The United Nations is the primary intergovernmental source for cross-cutting global indicators.
sources.label: United Nations

sources.justification: The World Bank is the reference publisher for global development and economic indicators.
sources.label: World Bank

sources.justification: The OECD publishes authoritative comparative economic and social statistics.
sources.label: OECD

sources.justification: Only EU institutions use europa.eu, so the domain itself establishes institutional authority.
sources.label: European Union

sources.justification: The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights is the authority for human-rights and atrocity indicators.
sources.label: UN Human Rights (OHCHR)

sources.justification: The UN Refugee Agency is the authority for forced-displacement and refugee figures.
sources.label: UNHCR

sources.justification: UNESCO is the UN specialized agency for education, cultural, and scientific indicators.
sources.label: UNESCO

sources.justification: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology authored the AI Risk Management Framework, the original anchor for technological claims.
sources.label: NIST

sources.justification: The UK AI Security Institute is a government AI risk research body; official quantified sources are scarce in this category, and without it technological claims always quarantine.
sources.label: UK AI Security Institute

sources.justification: The OECD AI Policy Observatory is the intergovernmental reference for AI policy indicators.
sources.label: OECD.AI

sources.justification: The International Telecommunication Union is the UN specialized agency for ICT and AI standards, and publishes the Global Cybersecurity Index.
sources.label: ITU

sources.justification: The Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System is UN/EU-backed and the primary real-time disaster alerting feed for World Pulse events.
sources.label: GDACS

sources.justification: ReliefWeb is UN OCHA's humanitarian crisis reporting service and the reference feed for displacement and response figures.
sources.label: ReliefWeb

sources.justification: The International Monetary Fund is the authority for the economic event category, the same institutional tier as worldbank.org and oecd.org.
sources.label: IMF

sources.justification: The Bank of Korea is South Korea's central bank and the national monetary authority; its own statements on market volatility and rate decisions are the authoritative primary source for the economic event category, the same institutional tier as a national central bank cited under the economic-event allowlist rule.
sources.label: Bank of Korea

sources.justification: South Korea's Ministry of Economy and Finance is the national government agency that convenes and publishes official readouts of emergency market-stabilization meetings, making it the authoritative primary source for government intervention in the economic event category.
sources.label: Ministry of Economy and Finance (Korea)

sources.justification: Encyclopaedia Britannica has a stable named editorial board accountable for its entries, unlike community-edited references.
sources.label: Encyclopaedia Britannica

sources.justification: The Smithsonian Institution is a US national museum and research complex with curatorial accountability for its published figures.
sources.label: Smithsonian Institution

sources.justification: The Library of Congress is the US national library and a primary-source custodian.
sources.label: Library of Congress

sources.justification: The US National Archives is the custodian of US federal primary records.
sources.label: U.S. National Archives

sources.justification: The UK National Archives is the custodian of UK government primary records.
sources.label: UK National Archives

sources.justification: The British Museum publishes curatorial scholarship on antiquity with named institutional accountability.
sources.label: British Museum

sources.justification: The Metropolitan Museum of Art publishes peer-reviewed curatorial scholarship, including its Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History.
sources.label: The Metropolitan Museum of Art

sources.justification: Our World in Data is a curated research dataset publisher at the University of Oxford with documented sourcing for every series.
sources.label: Our World in Data

sources.justification: Cambridge University Press is a peer-reviewed academic publisher.
sources.label: Cambridge University Press

sources.justification: Oxford University Press is a peer-reviewed academic publisher; academic.oup.com matches as a subdomain.
sources.label: Oxford University Press

sources.justification: JSTOR hosts peer-reviewed scholarly literature with stable citations.
sources.label: JSTOR

sources.justification: The US National Institutes of Health publishes biomedical research and historical epidemiology.
sources.label: NIH

sources.justification: The US National Library of Medicine holds the medical-history collections; a finer label than nih.gov, which it also matches as a subdomain.
sources.label: U.S. National Library of Medicine

sources.justification: The US Holocaust Memorial Museum is the reference institution for Holocaust documentation and death-toll scholarship.
sources.label: US Holocaust Memorial Museum

sources.justification: Imperial War Museums is the UK national institution for twentieth-century conflict records.
sources.label: Imperial War Museums

sources.justification: The US Office of the Historian publishes the official Foreign Relations of the United States documentary record.
sources.label: U.S. Office of the Historian
